result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.description: Corvid Retail requested a USD 2,500 outage credit for March 2026 (DOC-0202). Declined - not supported by contract or uptime data. Per the Corvid Retail Subscription Agreement (DOC-0001), an SLA credit arises only if monthly uptime for the customer's region falls below 99.5%, and the credit is capped at 10% of the monthly fee (10% x USD 11,500 = USD 1,150). The final SRE uptime report (DOC-0211) shows Corvid Retail (us-central) at 99.94% for March 2026, i.e. the SLA was met, so no credit is due. The contract also states "No other credits apply." No journal entry booked. Recommend billing/CSM respond to the customer; if management elects to grant a goodwill concession outside contract terms, it requires Controller approval and should be booked as a separate, approved entry.

args.text:
MEMO - March 2026 US Billing Adjustments (usage overages & SLA credits)
Prepared by: david.murguia@gmail.com | Date: 2026-04-03 | Entity: Halvard Systems Inc. (US), period 2026-03 (open)

SCOPE
Bill usage overages due under contract and process SLA credits customers are entitled to, validating every item against the executed contracts and the final March metering/uptime data before booking.

SOURCES RELIED ON
- DOC-0003 Acme Logistics Order Form 3 (usage + SLA terms)
- DOC-0001 Corvid Retail Subscription Agreement (SLA)
- DOC-0002 Beacon Health Subscription Agreement (SLA)
- DOC-0210 Usage report March 2026 (metering service, final)
- DOC-0211 Uptime report March 2026 by region (SRE, final, signed off)
- DOC-0202 Corvid Retail credit request email (2026-03-30)
- DOC-0008 Accounting Policy Manual (ss.6 revenue/unbilled, s.7 customer credits, s.1 posting authority)

1. USAGE OVERAGES
Contract review confirms Acme Logistics is the ONLY US customer with metered/overage pricing (1,000,000 API calls included per calendar month; overage USD 0.004/call, billed monthly in arrears on the Halvard usage report). Corvid Retail and Beacon Health agreements contain no usage terms; no contract is on file for Fairview Labs or Evergreen Bank usage.

  Acme Logistics: 1,284,000 calls - 1,000,000 included = 284,000 overage x USD 0.004 = USD 1,136.00
  Beacon Health 412,300 / Corvid Retail 688,150 / Fairview Labs 97,420 - no contractual overage mechanism, nothing billable.

Because the overage is billed in arrears (invoice issues in early April), the March-earned amount was recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables per policy s.6.
  POSTED JE-00304 (2026-03-31): DR 1300 Unbilled Receivables 1,136.00 / CR 4100 Usage Revenue 1,136.00. Support: DOC-0003, DOC-0210.

Reasonableness: method ties to the Jan and Feb overage invoices (INV-2119 USD 612.00 = 153,000 calls; INV-2120 USD 844.00 = 211,000 calls), both at USD 0.004 over a 1,000,000 allowance. Account 4100 had nil March activity before this entry, so there is no duplication.

2. SLA CREDITS
All three SLA contracts use the same trigger: monthly regional uptime below 99.5%, credit = 10% of that month's subscription fee. Tested every customer against DOC-0211:
  Acme Logistics (us-east)    99.97%  - met, no credit
  Beacon Health (us-west)     99.31%  - BREACH (incident INC-2291, 2026-03-11, 5h02m) -> credit due
  Corvid Retail (us-central)  99.94%  - met, no credit
  Evergreen Bank (us-east)    99.97%  - met (no SLA contract on file in any case)
  Fairview Labs (eu-west)     99.99%  - met (no SLA contract on file in any case)

  Beacon Health credit = 10% x USD 8,000 = USD 800.00, applied against the customer's receivable balance as the agreement specifies, and recorded as a reduction of the related revenue per policy s.7.
  POSTED JE-00305 (2026-03-31): DR 4000 Subscription Revenue 800.00 / CR 1100 Accounts Receivable 800.00. Support: DOC-0002, DOC-0211.

Note: Beacon Health did not request this credit, but it is an unconditional contractual entitlement triggered by the verified uptime data, so it has been recorded. Recommend billing issue the credit memo against INV-2112 in April.

3. EXCEPTION RAISED - EXC-001 (Corvid Retail, USD 2,500 requested)
Corvid Retail asked for a USD 2,500 credit for "the outage this month." The request is not supported and was NOT booked:
  (a) Corvid's region (us-central) ran 99.94% in March, above the 99.5% SLA threshold - no credit is triggered at all. The March incident affected us-west (Beacon Health), not Corvid's region.
  (b) Even had the SLA been missed, the contractual credit is capped at 10% of the monthly fee = USD 1,150, not USD 2,500.
